turns.t: Hi, doctor! I'm Priya, and I'm here for my epilepsy review, I've got so much to tell you, because I had a seizure, one, since my last visit, and I haven't stopped worrying about it.
Thank you for telling me. When was the seizure?
Six weeks ago, on a Tuesday night. I was asleep, my husband woke up and I was shaking. It lasted about two minutes, he said.
How did you feel afterwards?
Awful. Confused, exhausted, a headache, and I'd bitten my tongue. I slept for twelve hours.
Did anything seem to trigger it? ~
I'd missed two doses of my tablet that week, and I'd had a few late nights. And a glass of wine. ~
That's an honest answer, thank you. Any other seizures, or odd episodes like staring or jerking?
No. None. Nothing else.
Any injuries, falls, or fits during the day?
No.
What are you taking?
Lamotrigine, 150 mg, twice a day. I've been on it for four years.
Any side effects, rashes, dizziness, double vision?
No. Nothing like that.
Any other conditions?
Epilepsy since I was fifteen. And I'm planning a pregnancy next year, that's partly why I came.
Good thinking. Any operations?
My appendix, when I was twenty.
Let me check your reflexes and coordination, for completeness. ~
Okay.
Everything looks normal. Priya, a single seizure after missed doses and poor sleep isn't a failure of treatment. The tablet works, when it's taken regularly. ~
That's a relief. ~
I'm not going to change the dose, but I'd like you to set a phone alarm for both doses, and use a weekly pill box.
I'll do both. ~
Keep a regular sleep routine, limit alcohol, and avoid skipping meals.
Right. ~
For your pregnancy plans, lamotrigine is one of the safer options, but you'll need folic acid at a higher dose before you conceive, 5 mg once a day.
Five milligrams. Okay. I'll start it. ~
Please come and see me before you try, and tell the pharmacy you're planning a pregnancy.
I will. ~
Keep the driving restriction in mind, you must not drive for the period the rules set after a seizure. ~
Understood. ~
